triggerCases.prompt: Record a video of opening the settings menu and saving a change in Chrome.
Capture before and after videos of this drag-and-drop fix for the PR.
Use the existing Playwright setup to save a video of this Firefox bug reproduction.
Take a screenshot of the expanded menu for this PR at 320px wide.
Use Chrome DevTools Recorder to export a replayable checkout action script. I don't need a video.
Record a Chrome performance trace and identify what makes this page load slowly.

outputCases.prompt: Save a video of dragging the first card below the second card in the prepared Chrome page, with a visible cursor and no audio.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: An inspected native recording captures only the requested drag interaction and uses the prepared session without installing or uploading anything.
assertions: The workflow verifies the prepared page and uses its available native recorder rather than creating a new browser context or falling back to recordVideo.
Recording starts after setup, the real drag moves the first card below the second, and stop runs even if the interaction fails.
The output uses an absolute temporary MP4 path, requests no audio, and verifies the client's supported cursor overlay appears without modifying application styles.
The workflow plays the saved video or reports limited frame-based inspection, and does not treat a 60fps request or metadata alone as proof of 60 distinct frames per second.
Delivery identifies the source, route, viewport, and captured interaction, discloses the cursor overlay, and performs no package installation or external write.

outputCases.prompt: Record the save interaction using the exposed Chrome tools and return the video.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: The exposed recorder is used within its documented capabilities, without an unsupported claim that it uses Chrome's native recording API.
assertions: The workflow reads the exposed start/stop schemas and uses the matching existing page; it does not infer a backend from the screencast_start name or MP4 extension.
The workflow records and finalizes the save interaction using the exposed tools instead of installing chrome-capture or requiring a raw protocol connection.
The workflow inspects the actual output and reports the unknown backend and any unverified audio/cursor behavior without claiming 120fps, native encoding, or desktop coverage.
The response returns the local recording and does not upload it or change source or configuration.

outputCases.prompt: Save a video of the menu bug using the installed browser tools. Keep my existing tab open.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: The available Playwright recorder captures the interaction in a separate context, preserves the user's tab, and reports the actual fallback and verification limits.
assertions: The workflow recognizes the missing native protocol command and uses the existing Playwright recording capability without downloading a package, upgrading Chrome, or changing global configuration.
The workflow creates a separate context with recordVideo enabled, repeats the permitted setup, reproduces the bug, and closes only its own context to finalize the video.
The user's original tab and context remain open and unchanged, and the delivered format is WebM rather than an asserted native AV1 MP4.
The workflow inspects available frames and metadata, explicitly reports that continuous motion and audio playback were not verified, and makes no claim about distinct frame rate.
